newsitem.title: CANADA: Arakis Energy appoints U.K. adviser.
newsitem.headline: Arakis Energy appoints U.K. adviser.

text.p: Canada's Arakis Energy Corp said on Friday that it appointed Robert Fleming & Co Ltd to advise it and participate on its behalf in negotiating detailed operating provisions for its US$1 billion Sudan oil joint venture.

Arakis said that the British merchant bank's energy group would also advise it in seeking an international appraisal to assess additions to the value of the Sudan Petroleum Project between 1993 and 1996.

Arakis said last week it signed an interim agreement to forge a joint venture for developing its 12.2-million-acre southern Sudan oil concession and build a 950-mile pipeline to the Red Sea. The consortium aims to begin shipping 150,000 barrels of oil per day in 1999.
The partners included Arakis with 25 percent, Malaysia's Petronas with 40 percent, China National Petroleum Corp with 30 percent and the Sudan government with five percent.

Under the deal, Arakis subsidiary State Petroleum was expected to remain as operator for the project until the signing of a formal agreement, which would transfer operatorship to a joint operating company.
Arakis said formal agrements were expected to be completed in March. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
